introduction.text: The Fontana dell'Acqua Paola is a monumental fountain on Rome's Janiculum Hill that commemorates the restoration of the Acqua Paola aqueduct by Pope Paul V in 1612. It is significant for providing clean water to the city, influencing later fountains such as the Trevi Fountain, and displaying papal authority through its iconography.

history.description: The Acqua Traiana aqueduct was originally built by Emperor Trajan in 109 CE and later restored by Pope Paul V.
The Fontana dell'Acqua Felice was built by Pope Sixtus V between 1585 and 1588, inspiring the design of the Fontana dell'Acqua Paola.
The Fontana dell'Acqua Paola was constructed in 1612 to mark the completion of the Acqua Paola aqueduct.
In 1690, Carlo Fontana designed an additional semicircular pool for the fountain.
An ordinance issued in 1707 forbade residents from bathing in the fountain.
In 2019, a Fendi-sponsored campaign funded a partial renovation of the fountain.

design.description: Giovanni Fontana and Flaminio Ponzio designed the fountain, featuring a massive gateway of five arches that channel water into five marble basins.
White marble from the ruins of the Roman Temple of Minerva in the Forum of Nerva was used in the construction.
Atop the fountain, a papal tiara and keys, the Borghese family coat of arms, and angels support the inscription praising Pope Paul V.

art.description: The fountain’s theme focuses on water, with five streams pouring through arches into marble basins and an additional semicircular pool added in 1690.
An inscription atop the fountain praises Pope Paul V for bringing water to the residents of the Janiculum Hill.
Iconographic elements include the papal tiara, keys, Borghese coat of arms, and angels.
